summary.change: Add a single 'affected modules' query — given one or more changed module IDs, answer with every module that depends on them directly or transitively, plus the changed modules themselves — answered from the dependency facts a project's retained analysis session already keeps for its own fast incremental invalidation (not the separate, process-spawned dependency-diagram/visualization analyzer). Offer the query through four surfaces: the ramify/analysis retained-session API itself, the daemon's context-level query surface, the daemon client/service protocol, the ramify CLI, and (newly) an MCP tool module, all reading one stated revision without re-analyzing.
preserves: No importability rule changes: the query only reports existing dependency facts, it does not alter what any module may import.
No dependency graph is kept between queries; each answer is derived fresh from the current published revision's already-retained facts, never accumulated across queries.
Ordinary checks and hooks (RetainedSession.update/sweep) do no added work: the new query reads already-computed facts and never triggers them.
The existing dependencyDiagram/dependencyFacts capability (process-spawned analyzer, used for the presentation/explorer visualization) is left untouched and is not the mechanism for this query.

modulesTouched.why: Owns RetainedSession and its retained per-revision incremental facts (catalogs, descriptions, model decisions) used to decide unchanged-surface vs. source-path re-checks; must add the new query as a RetainedSession capability that classifies edges as ordinary/type-only/test/declaration-level and computes the reverse transitive closure from already-retained facts, reporting incompleteness when its own coverage is partial.

Drives one retained analysis session per context and already answers other per-revision queries (apiView, architectView, measurements, dependencyDiagram) straight from the published revision; needs a symmetrical 'affectedModules' context query that calls the new RetainedSession capability and republishes coverage/limits, without starting new analysis.

Owns the validated in-process service, its request/response vocabulary, capability negotiation and the daemon client; needs a new service operation and capability name (alongside the existing dependencyDiagram, materialize-views, measure capabilities) and client-side plumbing to reach the new context query.

Assembles the CLI, daemon and (new) MCP entry points from their owners and defines the dispatch-facing service vocabulary the daemon implements; needs to add the new query's request/response shape to that shared vocabulary and wire the new MCP module in alongside the CLI.

Parses arguments and reaches the daemon through an injected connector; needs one new subcommand that sends the affected-modules request and formats the module list plus coverage/limits, reusing the existing connector and report-formatting machinery.

New module: exposes the affected-modules query (and, if bundled, the same daemon-backed queries) as an MCP tool for agent post-write hooks, reusing the existing daemon client to reach the resident daemon.

assumed: The 'retained-session API' the plan names is ramify/analysis's exposed RetainedSession interface, and its per-revision incremental catalogs (used to decide unchanged-surface vs. source-path re-checks in update()/sweep()) are the 'dependency facts... kept for fast incremental checks' the plan requires the answer to come from, distinct from the process-spawned dependencyDiagram/dependencyFacts analyzer used for presentation.

Because the project has no MCP-serving module today, delivering the query over MCP requires one new module, proposed here as ramify/mcp, a sibling of ramify/cli under the root, reusing the existing daemon client rather than duplicating daemon-reaching logic.

The CLI is the most representative entry point for the plan's stated CI/hook use case, so it is named as the map's entry point even though the daemon client, retained-session API and MCP tool are equally valid callers of the same underlying query.

Coverage granularity (ordinary/type-only/test/declaration) is assumed to require an extension of ramify/analysis's dependency classification beyond the existing DependencyBoundaryFact's behavioral/non-behavioral split, since that split does not itself distinguish those four kinds.
notFound: No existing module named for MCP, or any headline/symbol mentioning MCP or the Model Context Protocol, anywhere in the 15-module architect view — absence here is direct (README lists every module and its purpose) rather than a coverage gap.

No existing RetainedSession method or test suite named affectedModules, dependents, or similar in ramify/analysis's exposed symbols or test suites — treated as evidence the capability is genuinely new, though the view's 366-symbol cut means some undocumented internal helper could exist unseen.

No exposed function on RetainedSession that already surfaces per-file or per-module import edges for external querying (only apiView, architectView, measurements and explorerDetails suites were found); the incremental catalogs are assumed to exist internally (they are described in prose as bounding 'the checked set') but their exact shape was not established because RetainedSession's full signature is cut in the view.

evidence.claim: The project has 15 modules rooted at ramify, matching this job's stated evidence.
ramify/analysis owns RetainedSession, an exposed interface reexposed by the root to all descendants, whose revisions recompute only the facts a change reaches.
RetainedSession already exposes apiView, architectView, measurements and explorerDetails as queryable capabilities answered from a published revision without a new report or rescan.

The existing dependencyDiagram/dependencyFacts capability is computed by spawning a separate analyzer process per run (createProcessDependencyAnalyzer), not by reusing already-retained incremental facts, so it is not the mechanism this plan's query should reuse.

ramify/daemon/contexts already answers other per-revision queries (apiView, architectView, dependencyDiagram) straight from one context's published revision without rereading project files, and never keeps a graph between queries.
ramify/daemon owns the validated daemon service, its capability negotiation (dependencyDiagram, materialize-views, measure capability names) and the daemon client connectDaemon.
ramify/daemon/contexts's own src API view lists RetainedSession as an available type-only import from ramify/analysis.
ramify/daemon's own src API view lists ContextManager and createContextManager as available imports from its contexts child.
ramify/cli's own src API view lists connectDaemon as an available import from ramify/daemon.
No module in the project's 15-module tree is named or described as an MCP surface; the request's fourth delivery surface (MCP) does not yet exist and must be proposed.

The root module ramify assembles the command line, resident daemon and lazy batch analysis from its owners and defines the dispatch-facing service vocabulary the daemon implements, making it the natural place to add the new query's shared request/response shape and wire in a new MCP entry point.
